next_guide.basis: Revenue/billings guide was raised in May and August, Q2 beat the top of guidance by ~$30m and Jefferies' field checks put calendar Q3 slightly above company forecasts, so a revenue raise is the base case; the EPS range was only narrowed last time and the largest EBA renewal cohort sits in Q4, so an EPS/FCF guide held flat is the main risk, plus any first FY28 framework without the transaction-model lift.

evidence.text: Earnings Whispers carries a whisper EPS of $3.16 against consensus $3.07 and the company's guide of $3.04-3.09, so the market bar sits ~2% above the top of guidance; a Q2-sized beat (EPS +5.8%, $3.30 vs $3.12) clears it, a smaller beat does not.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 and Q2 FY27 both beat EPS and revenue above guidance and fell -4.0% and -3.67%; Q3 FY26 beat and rose +2.36%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is the bar, not an unpriced fact; filed because it says a guide-top beat is already expected. If the market expected only an in-line print, the whisper would sit at or below consensus.
evidence.independence: Jefferies (2026-11-09) also expects results without major surprises, which supports a beat being the base case (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-11-09-jefferies-releve-son-objectif-de-cours-sur-autodesk.html).

evidence.text: The stock went into the print about 25% above its Sep 9 low of $206.62 (now $258.57, 20d +6.8%), after a 16.6% fall in eight sessions following the Q2 beat-and-raise; part of a good Q3 is now in the price, though it is still ~17% below its 52w high and down ~12-14% YTD against SPY +6.7%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 went in after a run and sold off 3.67% on the window, then 16.6% more over eight days.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price itself; what it changes is the bar. Had the market been left skeptical, the stock would sit near the September low with a heavy put skew; it sits 25% higher with a skew of only +1.88.
evidence.independence: Jefferies notes ~25% rise since the quarter began (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-11-09-jefferies-releve-son-objectif-de-cours-sur-autodesk.html); baseline 20d +6.8%.

evidence.text: The last two prints (May and August 2026) beat revenue and EPS above the top of guidance and raised revenue guidance, yet fell -4.0% and -3.67% because the full-year EPS guide stayed at or below street ($12.52-12.60 vs $12.60) and margin guidance was held at ~39%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS guide below street: -3.67% (Aug 2026), -4.0% (May 2026). EPS guide not an issue: +5.32% (Feb 2026), +2.36% (Nov 2025).
evidence.why_not_priced: A reaction pattern, not a fact the market lacks; it tells the judges that a revenue beat-and-raise alone has not been bought this year. If the market had learned it, the whisper would not sit above the guide.
evidence.independence: SiliconANGLE 2026-08-27: shares -5% after hours as cash-flow guidance narrowed (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/autodesk-shares-fall-despite-q2-beat-as-cash-flow-guidance-narrows/); baseline history.

evidence.text: Jefferies (Nov 9) raised its target to $325 from $300 and said its field checks show calendar-Q3 activity slightly above the company's forecasts, with growth steady into 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Above-guide quarters were sold twice in 2026 (-4.0%, -3.67%) and bought in Nov 2025 (+2.36%).
evidence.why_not_priced: A published sell-side check is partly priced (stock +25% since); what is not priced is the size: 'slightly above company forecasts' fits the whisper rather than beating it. Snippet_only: the page answered 403.
evidence.independence: Procore's Q3 above-guide bookings (https://finviz.com/news/415677/procore-beats-as-organic-growth-accelerates-for-a-third-straight-quarter-but-the-dronedeploy-deal-changes-the-balance-sheet) point the same way on construction.

evidence.text: Loop Capital upgraded ADSK from Hold to Buy on 2026-11-13 (close $264.43); Fintel mean target $318.06.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history on analyst actions; the stock fell 3.88% on Nov 17, two sessions after the upgrade (AAII).
evidence.why_not_priced: Public and largely priced; filed because a pre-print upgrade marks sentiment going in. Snippet_only (page 503).
evidence.independence: Jefferies target raise 2026-11-09 (shared sentiment, different firm).

evidence.text: Procore (Q3 reported Nov 3, covering Jul-Sep) grew revenue 19% to $402m against a $382-384m guide, raised full-year revenue by ~$21m organically, cited stronger bookings, and called the construction environment unchanged from the prior quarter; organic growth accelerated for a third quarter and the stock rose 11%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Construction >20% was a supporting line in the Q2 beat that was sold (-3.67%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer read-through three weeks old and partly in ADSK's November high ($279); not in the ADSK consensus, which sits at the guide midpoint. Construction is a minority of ADSK revenue, so the net read is smaller than Procore's own beat.
evidence.independence: Bentley (infrastructure) and Trimble AECO ARR +13% (separate documents) point the same way; AIA billings point the other way.
evidence.link: Direct competitor in construction management software: Autodesk Construction Cloud vs Procore; Autodesk's construction business grows 'north of 20%' (Q2 call); same customers (GCs, owners), same quarter (Procore Jul-Sep vs ADSK Aug-Oct, two overlapping months).

evidence.text: Bentley Systems (Q3 reported Nov 5) grew ARR 13% in constant currency, raised its full-year ARR growth outlook to 12.5-13.5%, and reported net revenue retention of 110%, a historical high.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific; AECO revenue +17% in Q2 FY27.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer signal on infrastructure demand; partly priced. If the market doubted AECO demand, ADSK would not have recovered 25% from the September low alongside peers.
evidence.independence: SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1 of the same release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031308/000103130826000032/a26q3exhibit991.htm): same document.
evidence.link: Infrastructure design software (OpenRoads/MicroStation vs Civil 3D/AutoCAD), shared civil engineering and infrastructure customers within ADSK's AECO line (~half of ADSK revenue).

evidence.text: Trimble (Q3 reported Nov 4): AECO ARR a record $1.636bn, +13%, AECO revenue +9%, but total organic ARR growth outlook cut to 10% (from 12-14%), partly a $20m white-label shift and weaker positioning/transportation; EPS guide slightly raised.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mixed: the AECO line, which overlaps ADSK, is healthy; the cut is in non-overlapping lines. Net close to zero.
evidence.independence: Trimble 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000864749/000086474926000119/a2026q3-8kex991.htm): same document.
evidence.link: AECO software peer (Tekla, SketchUp, Viewpoint vs Revit, ACC); AECO is ~65% of Trimble ARR; overlapping construction customers.

evidence.text: Nemetschek (Q3 reported ~Nov 5) grew organic constant-currency revenue 12.5%, below its reaffirmed 14-15% full-year target, with a slower subscription transition in its Design segment; the shares fell more than 8%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific; Western Europe was ADSK's laggard on the Q2 call.
evidence.why_not_priced: Read-through on European design demand; ADSK held its range after it, so either discounted or not transmitted. Organic growth below target at a Europe-heavy design peer is a real negative signal for ADSK's Western Europe line, which is a minority of revenue.
evidence.independence: MarketBeat transcript highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-nemetschek-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-05/): same event.
evidence.link: Direct competitor in building design (Graphisoft/Vectorworks/Allplan vs Revit/AutoCAD), heavy in Western Europe, the region where ADSK said new-business productivity recovers slowest.

evidence.text: AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index read 44.9 for October 2026 (44.7 September), more than four years without sustained growth; inquiries rose but newly signed design contracts kept declining.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: ABI has been below 50 through every ADSK print in the baseline, including the +9.09% and +5.32% ones.
evidence.why_not_priced: Proxy; ADSK's subscription revenue has decoupled from ABI for years. Filed small.
evidence.independence: AIA infographic PDF (https://www.aia.org/sites/default/files/2026-11/RP26_ABI_08-2026-NOV.pdf): same source.
evidence.link: Architects are core Revit/AutoCAD seat buyers within AECO; macro proxy, not confirmed by ADSK, which grew AECO 17% in Q2 through the same weak ABI.

evidence.text: Autodesk raised FY27 revenue guidance at both prior prints (May: to $8,155-8,215m; August: underlying ~2pt billings raise, revenue to $8,295-8,345m incl. MaintainX) and beat the top of the Q2 revenue guide by ~$30m; a Q3 beat of similar size would support a further revenue/billings raise in the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue raises in May and August were sold (-4.0%, -3.67%) because EPS did not follow; Nov 2025 Q3 raise bought +2.36%.
evidence.why_not_priced: A raise is the base case; what is not priced is whether EPS follows. Filed small and positive because the Q3 quarter is where ADSK raised and was bought last year.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY27 release (https://finviz.com/news/357930/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results) records the May raise; Jefferies checks above company forecasts.

evidence.text: Management said on the Q2 call that the new transaction model added ~2pts to Q2 revenue growth and ~1.5pts to FY27 and will not recur, that FY28 revenue and FCF are 'too early' to frame, and only that FY28 non-GAAP margin improves modestly from 39% despite a full year of MaintainX costs; a first FY28 framework on this call would show the lift dropping out.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance lines decided the last two reactions (-4.0%, -3.67%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Known from August (Trefis framed it on Sep 10), but no FY28 street figure was found, so the bar is unknown; a framework implying low-teens organic growth would land on a stock rallied 25%. Whether ADSK gives FY28 colour in Q3 is not established.
evidence.independence: Trefis 2026-09-10 (https://www.trefis.com/articles/614900/why-did-autodesk-stock-drop-so-soon-after-raising-its-forecast/2026-09-10) reads the same comments; same underlying statement.

evidence.text: Billings lagged revenue in Q2 FY27 (billings +10% reported/+12% cc vs revenue +16%/+14% cc), cRPO growth slowed to 12% from 18-20%, total RPO +2% on reduced multiyear discounts; billings are the line the stock is now judged on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 billings/cRPO deceleration accompanied the -3.67% reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public numbers; filed because the comparison in Q3 is the question. The company attributes the RPO drag to multiyear wind-down and calls it temporary.
evidence.independence: SiliconANGLE Q2 coverage with RPO $7.433bn +2%, cRPO $5.245bn +12% (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/autodesk-shares-fall-despite-q2-beat-as-cash-flow-guidance-narrows/).

evidence.text: Q2 FY27 buyback was ~2.1m shares for $453m ($901m in H1); FY27 repurchase dollars guided equal to FY26 and ~50% of FCF; the stock traded near $206-230 for much of fiscal Q3, so the Q3 share count likely fell further.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a reaction line for this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Within guided capital return; inside the EPS guide. Small.
evidence.independence: Q2 release cash-flow statement ($901m six-month repurchases) (https://finviz.com/news/386371/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-second-quarter-results).

evidence.text: Short interest 9.2m shares (4.4% of shares outstanding), 6.1 days to cover, up 130.5k shares at the 2026-11-13 settlement; skew +1.88 vol points, put/call OI 0.93.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not available.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price; mildly rising shorts and a mild put premium say a modest bearish tilt with no squeeze setup either way. Snippet-level data.
evidence.independence: MarketWatch quote page listed the same 9.2m / 6.1 days with a different settlement date (snippet); AltIndex 9.38m / 4.57 days (https://altindex.com/ticker/adsk/short-interest).

evidence.text: FY27 carries Autodesk's largest-ever EBA renewal cohort, concentrated in Q4, while last year's largest cohort was product subscriptions, making H2 billings comparisons harder; Western Europe new-business productivity was recovering slowest after the sales reorganization.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Billings-quality commentary accompanied the August selloff.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management disclosed it; the risk is that a Q4 EBA-heavy guide keeps billings and FCF guide unraised. Shares a document with the FY28 finding but a different line (Q4 billings vs FY28 growth).
evidence.independence: Trefis 2026-11-16 names Q4 EBA renewals and Western Europe as the items to watch (https://www.trefis.com/stock/adsk/articles2/625194/how-much-should-one-lagging-number-worry-autodesk-stock-holders/2026-11-16).

evidence.text: MaintainX (closed Aug 3, ~$3.6bn cash) adds ~$60m revenue and ~$70m billings in H2, slightly Q4-weighted, and is reported separately for four quarters, so Q3 is the first print where organic growth can be read net of it; it dilutes margin.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First print with the acquisition; no history.
evidence.why_not_priced: The separate disclosure removes the cover for a soft core; ~$28-30m in Q3 is ~1.4% of revenue, so a headline beat smaller than that is an organic miss of the guide's spirit. Either direction.
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript gives the $60m/$70m H2 figures (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262137253-tradingkey).

evidence.text: PTC (fiscal Q4 to Sep 30, reported Nov 4) grew ARR ex-divested businesses 8% (9.7% cc) to ~$2.51bn and beat EPS ($2.03 vs $2.00); it no longer guides because of the pending $22.6bn Schneider Electric takeover announced Oct 5.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific.
evidence.why_not_priced: Steady manufacturing demand signal, small and partly priced.
evidence.independence: 247wallst summary of the same release (https://247wallst.com/cards/ptc-q4-2026-earnings-ptc-01m6m654wgxmzecr7rwafk0mdx).
evidence.link: Manufacturing design/PLM peer (Creo/Onshape vs Fusion/Inventor) in ADSK's Make/manufacturing line (Make revenue $244m in Q2, ~12% of total); the takeover also marks a private-market valuation for design software.

evidence.text: On the 2026-09-03 call management said Q4 FY27 (Jan quarter) should follow 'regular seasonality' only 'barring any memory impact', that it was still checking with customers whether they could secure enough memory for Q4, and that the 10-15% FY27 growth target was 'still a little uncertain'. With $328.0m booked through the Q3 midpoint, that target implies Q4 of $101-121m against a street of about $112.6m (~-6% q/q), so a memory-hit Q4 guide would land below the street.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the guide: Q3 FY26 (Nov 2025) fell 18.78% on a lower gross margin guide despite a beat; Q1 FY27 (May 2026) fell 21.41% on a cautious outlook with memory-inflation worries; Q2 FY27 with an in-line Q3 guide moved -0.77% (baseline and https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/AMBA).
evidence.why_not_priced: The memory caveat is public, and the 27.5% 20-day fall at a 52-week low prices a good part of it. What is not priced is the size: the street's ~$112.6m Q4 still assumes normal seasonality, and an implied FY27 of ~$441m sits at the top half of a 10-15% range management called uncertain. If the market had fully priced a memory cut, the Q4 and FY estimates would have come down toward $105m and $433m, and they have not visibly moved.
evidence.independence: The company's own words; corroborated in direction by peer and counterparty evidence filed separately (GoPro 10-Q memory price spike, Himax Q4 guide), which are different documents. The FY27 10-15% frame comes from https://finance.yahoo.com/news/ambarella-reaffirms-fy2027-growth-edge-011831748.html (2026-03-11).

evidence.text: Earnings Whispers' 2026-11-16 preview reports days of inventory at 157 against 76 a year earlier, free cash flow negative in each of the last two quarters (IP licence payments and an inventory build), Q2 non-GAAP gross margin 59.3% below its guide midpoint after 59.9% the quarter before and 60.9% a year earlier, and says gross margin is 'the first place the bull case could crack'. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 print fell 18.78% on a lower gross margin guide after a revenue beat (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/11/26/why-ambarella-stock-just-crashed).
evidence.why_not_priced: Published and widely read, so mostly priced. What remains is whether the Q4 gross margin guide drops below 59% on mix or cost pass-through lag. Management said memory prices do not touch its own gross margin (it does not buy memory), which caps the risk.
evidence.independence: Inventory days (157 against 145 the quarter before) also come from the CFO's Q2 remarks summarised at https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262150875-tradingkey (same underlying company disclosure, so not independent).

evidence.text: Inventory days rose from 145 to 157 in Q2 FY27, while inventory dollars fell 4% q/q and DSO fell from 35 to 32. Cash fell from $277.8m to $272.3m. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned visibly on inventory alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for three months; small residual. If priced, the stock would not react to an inventory number in line with Q2's.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2 disclosure with the gross margin finding; counted once here, on the inventory line only.

evidence.text: GoPro's Q3 2026 10-Q says memory component costs rose sharply, including unexpected price increases of 70-80% in the last week of September 2026, and that it may not be able to offset them. GoPro's Q3 hardware revenue fell 49.5% and it gave no guidance. This is evidence that consumer camera OEMs, Ambarella's end market, were hit by a memory squeeze inside Ambarella's Q3 and going into its Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 fell 21.41% when a downgrade cited memory inflation in the tech supply chain (https://www.tikr.com/blog/ambarella-fell-21-today-heres-how-much-the-stock-could-rise-in-2026).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is in a 10-Q footnote of a company with no call and a pending merger, so it was barely covered; the 70-80% late-September step is dated after Ambarella last spoke (09-03) and its Citi appearance (09-17). It is a proxy, so it is small.
evidence.independence: Insta360's Q3 report also cites memory price rises squeezing profit (https://wap.eastmoney.com/a/202610273910539824.html), but its revenue still grew 33%, which cuts the other way on volume.
evidence.link: Same end product (action cameras, Ambarella's legacy IoT market). GoPro designs its own GP-series SoC, so it is not established as a current Ambarella customer; the link is the shared memory input and end market, not shared revenue.

evidence.text: Himax guided Q4 2026 revenue down 22-26% q/q on 2026-11-05, citing abrupt short-term order cuts and destocking by automotive customers, particularly Chinese automakers. Ambarella's automotive segment (about 22-25% of revenue, a record in Q2 FY27) sells ADAS and camera SoCs into the same Chinese and global auto supply chains.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto has been the growth line management highlights; no print in the baseline turned on auto alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a different company's segment, and Himax called auto 'relatively insulated from memory'; Ambarella's auto has run at records, so analysts are unlikely to have cut Ambarella's Q4 auto on a display-driver peer. Sized small as a segment proxy, net of IoT.
evidence.independence: Himax release headline: https://finviz.com/news/416607/himax-technologies-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-provides-fourth-quarter-2026-guidance (same event).
evidence.link: Both supply ICs to Chinese automakers' builds, but Himax sells display drivers (TDDI/DDIC), not perception SoCs. No shared named customer; auto is about a quarter of Ambarella's revenue, so the effect is net of the ~75% IoT side.

evidence.text: Insta360 (Arashi Vision, 688775.SH), whose cameras use Ambarella AI SoCs (cited in the ITC Insta360 case coverage), reported Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) revenue of RMB 3.919bn, up 33.3% y/y, with 9-month revenue up 42.7%, and said it increased inventory stocking (加大备货). Profit was squeezed by memory price rises. This overlaps two thirds of Ambarella's Aug-Oct quarter and supports IoT revenue at or above the guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ambarella prints revenue at its guide midpoint (Q1 FY27 $100.4m against $100.2m consensus, Q2 $108.1m against $108.03m); in-line revenue has not moved the stock up.
evidence.why_not_priced: A Shanghai STAR-market filing in Chinese, released after Ambarella last spoke; US coverage did not pick it up. It lands inside the guided Q3 range, so it supports a midpoint print more than a beat, which is why it is small. The growth slowed from +50% in H1 to +33%, and the stocking may pull Q4 demand forward.
evidence.independence: Hanwha Vision's record security quarter (separate finding, separate document) points the same way for IoT.
evidence.link: Insta360 360/action cameras use Ambarella AI SoCs (https://marketchameleon.com/PressReleases/i/2260942/AMBA/investor-alert-pomerantz-law-firm-investigates-claims, on the Feb 2026 ITC ruling); Insta360's share of Ambarella revenue is not disclosed (WT Microelectronics, the logistics partner, was 60.2% of Q2 revenue).

evidence.why_not_priced: A Korean filing read through Korean press; it supports professional security-camera demand despite memory costs. It lands inside the guided range.
evidence.independence: Insta360 finding (different end market, consumer cameras).

evidence.text: The same parent report shows asset quality turning in 3Q26. Argentina's NPL ratio was 6.0% at 30 Sep 2026, down 39bp in the quarter, and year-to-date cost of risk was 7.52%, down 19bp. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2Q26 NPL rose from 5.60% to 6.09% and coverage fell from 88% to 80% while the stock moved -0.9%. No clean record of the stock trading on an asset-quality improvement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sector sold off through November on macro (country risk 745 to 830-940), not on credit data. Goldman's NPL forecast of 5.9% is close to this, so it is partly in the bar. If the improvement were priced, the bank ADRs would not sit near 52-week lows with Goldman citing credit and capital concerns. Higher write-offs flatter the ratio and coverage is lower, so the improvement is real but of mixed quality.
evidence.independence: BCRA August 2026 bank report: system private NPL flat at 7.75% for four months and households slightly lower at 12.81% (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/publicaciones/informe-sobre-bancos-agosto-de-2026/). BCRA says the household irregular stock has fallen since August (https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/la-mora-bancaria-empieza-bajar-banco-central-ya-habla-fin-ciclo-atrasos-n101351). Shares a document with the previous finding, but a different line.

evidence.text: Expectations are already low. The stock is $9.42, -22.8% over 20 days (ARGT -19.4%, GGAL -25.1%), -57% from its 52-week high, 7.3% above its low, and below every analyst target found: Goldman Sell at $11.50 (cut from $13), UBS Neutral at $15 (cut from $20 on 2026-10-13), Benzinga mean $19. A disappointing quarter on the sell-side's own forecast meets a stock already marked down to it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a weak 1Q26 (-21% YoY) the stock rose +5.1% on 2026-05-27. After a strong 2Q26 it fell -0.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is sector-wide and macro-led: country risk rose and Milei's re-election odds fell. So the stock-specific bar may now sit below the published consensus. If the market had not marked it down, spot would sit near the targets rather than below Goldman's Sell target.
evidence.independence: ARGT and GGAL price paths from Yahoo (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ARGT?range=1mo&interval=1d). Sector YTD drawdowns at 29 Oct: BBAR -34.5%, GGAL -37.2%, BMA -33.3% (https://eleconomista.com.ar/finanzas/para-olvido-acciones-argentinas-desploman-42-dolares-ano-n99317).

evidence.text: Peer Grupo Supervielle reported 3Q26 on 2026-11-16. NIM fell to 16.0% from 20.3% and NII fell 22.4% QoQ because the 2Q gap between falling market rates and slower deposit-rate cuts closed, and because lower inflation cut CER/UVA income. It cut its 2026 real loan-growth guide to 0-5% from 10-15% and its ROE guide to 5-6% from 8-10%, and missed EPS consensus at $0.08 against $0.16. BBAR's NIM was 18.2% in 2Q26, with peso NIM at 21.8%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBAR's NIM moved from 18.6% to 18.2% in 2Q26 and the stock moved -0.9%. No record of the stock trading on NIM alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the print was public eight days before this one and Goldman models BBAR's NIM falling from 14.4% to 13%. Filed small as peer transmission.
evidence.independence: Guidance table at https://finsee.ai/earnings/supv/2026/q3/en/. The parent report's 'lower recurring revenue' for BBVA Argentina points the same way.
evidence.link: Same Argentine peso rate and inflation environment over the same quarter. Both are mid-to-large private banks with peso NIMs that benefited in 2Q26 from deposit-rate lag. BBAR guided its own NIM down about 100-200bp by year-end.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide from the 2Q26 call (real ROE low teens, about 10% real loan growth, cost of risk about 6.5%) is out of reach on the year-to-date numbers, so a cut is likely. ROE was 8.3% in Q1 and 12.2% in Q2, with Q3 near 8.8% on Goldman's forecast. The parent's report shows cost of risk at 7.52% year to date and lending up 23.4% in 9M against 23.6% inflation. The NPL guide of about 5.5% at year-end is the one line on track.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced record of BBAR's reaction to a guide cut.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. Goldman cut its 2026 earnings forecast by 18% and Supervielle cut across the board, so a cut is the base case. What is not known is its depth, and whether management resets 2027 (it guided system loan growth of 10-15% real for 2027). If the cut were fully priced, the street's Q4 estimate of $0.47 would sit below Q3's, not above it.
evidence.independence: BBVA parent 3Q26 report (https://shareholdersandinvestors.bbva.com/informes/3q26-report-business-areas-south-america/) and Supervielle's guide cuts (https://finsee.ai/earnings/supv/2026/q3/en/).

history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (8 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

options.event_implied_move_basis: 10.16% straddle over 24 calendar days less 24.86% of ordinary 20d-realised movement, subtracted in variance
options.skew_note: IV(25d put) - IV(25d call). Positive = the market is paying more for downside protection than for upside.

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 8 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: median historical reaction (no usable option chain)

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

evidence.text: BZ gapped down 23% on 2026-11-12, from $16.72 to an open of $13.95, with no company filing (MarketBeat). The 13.2% Q2 growth and 13.5% Q3 guide midpoint have not been contradicted by any company statement since 2026-08-25.

evidence.why_not_priced: The 23% gap priced a guidance disappointment that no document has confirmed. If the rumour were already fully reflected, the sector's 3% fall would not leave BZ 20 points behind it. Equally, the price would have retraced if the market saw the rumour as baseless, and it has not: the stock sits at the low. Either the guide confirms the rumour (little further downside) or it does not (a sharp retrace).
evidence.independence: 10jqka (2026-11-13, https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261113/c681791793.shtml) gives the same date and the sector/AI cause and notes fundamentals unchanged. September averaged 17.64 BTC/day at 36.0 EH/s against 20.46/day at 42.6 EH/s in June, bitcoin has fallen from about $83k at quarter-end to about $60k, and MARA sold post-quarter at about $81k. That puts Oct-Dec near 1,600 BTC times about $69k, roughly $110M. Any production or hashrate color on the call would therefore pull FY27 numbers down.

evidence.text: FQ4 mining revenue is mechanically about $122-125M against the $127.75M consensus (Yahoo, 14 analysts; Benzinga $126.3M), a miss of about 2-5%. The company's own monthly updates give 586 (Jul) + 593 (Aug) + 529 (Sep) = 1,708 BTC, down 11% from about 1,917 in FQ3 ($138.0M at about $72k revenue per BTC mined, CFO on the FQ3 call). Peers MARA and Riot realised $71,688 and $70,855 per BTC for the same Jul-Sep quarter, and CleanSpark ran about 1% above MARA in the prior quarter ($72k vs $71,325).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ3 revenue missed ($138.0M against $139-154M) and the stock fell 3.53%; FQ2 -5.8%. Revenue misses have drawn small negative reactions, not large ones.
evidence.why_not_priced: The production figures are public, but the consensus mean ($127.75M) still implies about $74.8k per BTC, above what either peer realised. If the street had priced the peers' Jul-Sep prices, the mean would sit near $123M and the range would not run to $158M. The miss is small and mostly inferable, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Production comes from the company's July (https://finviz.com/news/377574/cleanspark-releases-july-2026-operational-update) and August (https://finviz.com/news/389855/cleanspark-releases-august-2026-operational-update) updates. The prices are independent peer filings: MARA 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001507605/000150760526000028/mara-20260930.htm) and Riot's release (https://www.riotplatforms.com/riot-platforms-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-strategic-highlights/). The FQ3 per-BTC figure comes from the FQ3 transcript (https://s21.q4cdn.com/978676932/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Q3FY26-Financial-Results-Transcript.pdf).

evidence.text: GAAP net income will very likely be large and positive against a -$0.37 EPS consensus, because bitcoin rose about 42.7% in the Jul-Sep quarter (from about $58.4k to about $83k) while CleanSpark held 13,530-13,931 BTC, marked at about $58.5k at 06-30 ($814.9M for about 13.9k BTC). The gross gain is roughly $300M+, before losses on the written calls (700 BTC called away in September at an average $72,928). Headline wire snapshots will print an EPS 'beat'. The item sits below operating income and bitcoin has since fallen back to about $60k, so it has no path to the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MARA printed $632M of GAAP net income on an $885M bitcoin fair-value gain on 2026-11-09 and was little changed after hours. FQ3's $133M mark-to-market loss came with a -3.53% reaction, mostly attributed to the revenue miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street EPS strips the mark-to-market (Yahoo's FQ3 'actual' was -$0.39 against GAAP -$0.89), so headline EPS comparisons will read as a big beat. Professional holders know bitcoin's path, though, and the gain is already reversed by November, so this is a headline effect at most. If it were unpriced in a meaningful way, the EPS estimate would have been revised; it has not moved in 30 days.
evidence.independence: The holdings come from the company's 06-30 balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000827876/000119312526337999/clsk-ex99_1.htm) and September update. The analog is MARA's Q3 (https://theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-09-mara-q3-earnings-net-profit-bitcoin-sale-ai-pivot-436950).

evidence.text: Peer MARA reported the same Jul-Sep quarter on 2026-11-09 with revenue 22% below consensus ($164.2M vs $210.5M), an HPC lease timeline slipping toward 2027, and a GAAP profit on the bitcoin mark. It paired this with a $500M buyback and $750M of bitcoin-backed debt repaid from selling 13,597 BTC. The stock, sitting near its 52-week low of $5.69, rose about 10.5% the next day.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MARA's own reaction was flat to slightly down after hours on a miss, then +10.5% next day on the buyback news. CLSK's own November prints were +13.79% (2025-11-25), with +21.96% in February 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: MARA's reaction shows that a washed-out miner can rally on a miss when capital return is announced. CLSK has fallen a further about 25% since 11-16 with no company news, so no buyback is in its price. If the market expected a similar move, CLSK would not be sitting 2% above its 52-week low with put skew at 14 points.
evidence.independence: Separate source for the buyback and debt paydown: https://blockspace.media/insight/mara-buyback-bitcoin-debt-repayment/. CLSK has made no buyback statement, and finding 4 covers CLSK's own capacity; the two share no document.
evidence.link: Same business model and same quarter: both are US-listed bitcoin miners with large bitcoin treasuries (CLSK 13,530 BTC, MARA about 50k before the sale) pivoting to HPC leases, both with mining as essentially 100% of current revenue, and both trading near $5-7 at 52-week lows in November 2026. Same bitcoin price exposure, no shared customers.

evidence.text: CleanSpark has the means for a MARA-style capital action. The 2026-09-18/25 $2.276bn Sandersville notes (priced at 98.5%) were used partly to 'reimburse CleanSpark for certain prior equity contributions' (amount undisclosed), which returns cash to the parent, and management called Sandersville 'fully funded through completion'. The treasury holds 13,530 BTC, about $0.81bn at $60k, against a market cap of about $1.28bn at $5. Precedent: it repurchased 30.6M shares (10.9%) for $460M alongside the Nov-2025 convert.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov-2025 convert plus buyback was sold: the stock fell 10.13% on the pricing day, a different context because it came with $1.15bn of new debt. No standalone buyback reaction is on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: The reimbursement amount was never disclosed and the stock trades at a discount the treasury does not explain: bitcoin alone is about 63% of market cap, before $1.8bn of corporate debt. No sell-side note found mentions a buyback, and if one were expected the stock would not have fallen 25% in a week on no company news. It is inference, not a company statement, so it is sized small with a wide upper tail.
evidence.independence: The 'fully funded' quote comes from a different document, the September operational update (https://finviz.com/news/400827/cleanspark-releases-september-2026-operational-update). The 2025 buyback comes from The Block (https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2025-11-13-cleanspark-completes-upsized-convertible-notes-offering-378850).

evidence.text: The price path sets a low bar. CLSK fell 39.0% in 20 days and 18.8% in 5 days into the print, about twice bitcoin's roughly -21% from $76k to $60k over the same span, and sits 2% above its 52-week low. The decline came on the Texas governor result (-11% and -17% on 11-04/05) and on bitcoin, with no company-specific negative disclosure.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CLSK's two largest print reactions, +21.96% (Feb-2026) and +13.79% (Nov-2025), both came after drawdowns. The two most recent were -5.8% and -3.53%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the expectations state itself, not a hidden fact. Its information is that the stock has de-rated far more than its bitcoin holdings, so a merely non-catastrophic call is a lower bar than the consensus figures suggest. Against it, the skew says the options market still pays for downside.

evidence.text: A Texas lease announcement on this call is unlikely, and the market's bull case (Bernstein's $11 'depends on this lease') rests on it. The 885 MW Texas exclusivity with the Sandersville tenant began 2026-07-14 (CEO: 'an exclusivity window, not at the finish line', with industry windows of 30-120 days), so it is now about 133 days old. ERCOT moved final Batch Zero determinations to December 2026. Governor-elect Hinojosa, taking office 2027-01-19, wants new data center approvals paused. Riot signed its own Texas lease (910 MW, Corsicana) on 11-04.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Texas election news drove -11% and -17% on 11-04/05. The Sandersville lease announcement (2026-07-14) was a positive catalyst before the FQ3 print. No reaction to an exclusivity update on a call is on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: The election shock is priced. What may not be priced is that a call with no Texas signing, or with an exclusivity that is extended or quietly lapsed, removes the near-term catalyst the remaining holders are waiting for. If the market already assumed no lease before December, the stock would not have kept selling off into the print. Both tails are real, because a signing would be a large positive, so the range is wide.
evidence.independence: Exclusivity terms: FQ3 transcript (https://s21.q4cdn.com/978676932/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Q3FY26-Financial-Results-Transcript.pdf). Election and Bernstein dependence: https://www.tikr.com/blog/could-cleanspark-actually-climb-65-or-is-bernstein-totally-wrong. These are separate documents.

September production ran 17.64 BTC/day at 36.0 EH/s, down from 20.46/day at 42.6 EH/s in June, and the deployed fleet fell from 230,507 units (July) to 199,745 (September). Bitcoin went from about $83k at quarter-end to about $60k now, which gives roughly 1,600 BTC at about $69k average, near $110M. The Dec quarter will also carry a mark-to-market loss of roughly $300M on about 13.5k BTC. Any Oct-Nov production or hashrate color on the call pulls FY27 down.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No guide history, since the company does not guide. FY27 EPS has already been cut from -$1.02 to -$1.75 over three months (TIKR 11-16) with the stock falling throughout.
evidence.why_not_priced: Monthly updates ended in October, so the market has not seen October or November production or the treasury balance. The 9-analyst next-quarter mean has not been revised in 30 days and EPS for that quarter shows zero revisions. If the shortfall were priced, the estimate would sit near $110M. The stock's -39% suggests the price may already discount it even though the estimates do not, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: The hashrate and fleet figures come from the September operational update (https://finviz.com/news/400827/cleanspark-releases-september-2026-operational-update) and the June update (https://finviz.com/news/366291/cleanspark-releases-june-2026-operational-update). evidence.text: Mid-quarter statements: on 2026-10-09 the CEO said 'our Sandersville project is fully funded through completion' after closing $2.276bn of 7.875% senior secured notes at the project subsidiary, with no parent equity, consistent with the CFO's 08-06 pledge of no equity or equity-linked raise for Sandersville. The same release ended monthly operational updates. On 2026-11-06 the company announced investor events at Cantor (11-11), BofA Leveraged Finance and Chardan (12-01), and Wells Fargo (12-08).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August update (09-08) came on a -9.24% day. The September update and notes closing coincided with the stock's slide from about $11-12 to $8-9 into November.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced. It matters as a removal of equity-dilution risk for Sandersville: what the money buys is a contracted, investment-grade 20-year lease, so it reads as a positive or neutral [sizing note removed]. If dilution fear were still in the price, a 30% short base could partly reflect it, and the call can lay it to rest.
evidence.independence: Investor events: https://finviz.com/news/418630/cleanspark-announces-participation-in-upcoming-investor-events. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov-2025 convert led to -10.13% on pricing and about -30% over the week. The 2026-09 project notes drew no identifiable single-day reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Under LESSONS section 4 it is unsigned until its use is known. If the call ties it to a Texas lease it is positive; if it is unexplained parent leverage, negative. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Collateral figure from the September update (https://finviz.com/news/400827/cleanspark-releases-september-2026-operational-update). This shares the investor-events document with finding 9.

evidence.text: Bitcoin is at about $59.7k on 2026-11-24 (-3.5% in 24h), after six straight weekly losses, a Fear and Greed reading of 10, and about $1.9bn of November ETF outflows. evidence.why_not_priced: Bitcoin's level is fully priced and its next-day direction is not knowable, so this is [sizing note removed]. It is filed so the judges see that the dominant driver is exogenous. The price is a page ticker read on 11-24 (CoinGecko via cryptobriefing), snippet-level.

evidence.text: Deere's first FY27 net income guide is likely to land below the street's FY27 bar. Barchart consensus is $23.40 EPS (+29%, about $6.3bn at about 269m shares). Bernstein publicly forecasts $5.4bn / $20 (5-10% below consensus), and Oppenheimer sees limited room to beat. Deere's previous two first-year guides were set well below the street: FY25 at $5.0-5.5bn (midpoint EPS about $19 against $21.58 consensus) and FY26 at $4.0-4.75bn against $5.19bn consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first-year guide moved the stock both ways. On 2024-11-21 the FY25 guide was about 12% below the street but came with a large Q4 beat ($4.55 against $3.87), and the stock rose about 8% (Nasdaq/Citi, https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/citi-anticipates-deere-shares-react-positively-q4-beat). On 2025-11-26 the FY26 guide of $4.0-4.75bn was against $5.19bn consensus, and the stock fell 5.67% (sealed baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-deere-stock-dropped-today).
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline consensus still reads $23.40 (Barchart, 2026-11-22). If the market had fully adopted Bernstein's $20, the published mean would be near $21 and mean targets would not sit 12-15% above spot. The 9% pre-print slide and the put skew show it is partly priced.
evidence.independence: Bernstein's view and Oppenheimer's comment both come from TipRanks. Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/deere-earnings-up-next-can-guidance-ease-downturn-fears-93CH-5048535, 2026-11-24) carries Bernstein independently. The Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 guide gaps come from separate sources (Nasdaq/Citi; Bloomberg/Nasdaq).

evidence.text: Deere's CFO said on the Aug 20 call that FY27 tariff expense will run at about $1bn against about $750m net in FY26, a step-up of about $250m pre-tax (about 4% of FY26 net income after tax). The $382m of FY26 tariff refunds ($272m Q2 + $110m Q3) will not recur, and no refund is assumed in Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff costs ($1.2bn gross FY26) were cited in the Nov 2025 guide that sold off 5.7%. This line has not surprised on its own since.
evidence.why_not_priced: It has been public since August and is partly in the models. The street's +29% FY27 EPS growth is hard to reconcile with a $250m cost step-up plus the loss of refunds, which suggests some estimates do not fully carry it. If they did, consensus would sit nearer Bernstein's $20.
evidence.independence: The Q3 release (https://finviz.com/news/383975/deere-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-1379-billion) confirms $110m / $382m of refunds. OptionBeast (2026-11-21) also says the refunds are unlikely to recur in FY27. Both rest on the same Aug 20 company statements.

evidence.text: Inside the quarter, Deere recalled all remaining laid-off workers at Waterloo, Ottumwa, Dubuque and the Quad Cities (more than 275 at Waterloo) and is hiring more than 400 at Illinois, Iowa and Kansas plants, including Harvester Works (combines) and Seeding. A spokesperson said on 2026-10-07 that this is to 'build dealer inventory ahead of upcoming planting and harvest cycles' and to serve customers 'including future labor negotiations'. That points to higher early-FY27 production and better absorption than FY26's deliberate underproduction.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a production-rate statement in the baseline window. In Aug 2026, early-order commentary was called 'the most significant' item by Raymond James, and the stock rose 6.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was covered as labor and local news, not in sell-side previews, none of which mention it. Part of the build is a hedge ahead of the UAW contract expiring 2027-10-31, which UAW members declined to extend on 2026-08-23. So it is partly a one-time pre-build, not demand. Sized net of that.
evidence.independence: CNH reports positive MY27 order intake (finding 5). AEM October data show large tractors up (finding 7). The contract timing is from AgWeb/RTTNews (https://www.rttnews.com/3683707/uaw-members-reject-deere-contract-extension-offer.aspx).

evidence.text: On 2026-11-04 Deere announced it will close Ottumwa (windrowers and balers to Des Moines by 2027-2028) and end manufacturing at Hagie/Clarion (STS sprayers to Thibodaux by 2029). It said it is 'currently operating far below normal production volumes'. No charge was quantified; Q4 or FY27 restructuring charges are possible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline window.
evidence.why_not_priced: Any charge would be small against about $5bn of net income and is below the operating line. The 'far below normal volumes' quote is consistent with the known underproduction.
evidence.independence: None; one company statement.

evidence.text: CNH (Q3, 2026-11-09) said North American order intake for MY27 is modestly positive against MY26 and the ag industry is 'approaching the end of this cyclical trough'. It cut ag dealer inventory by about $100m in Q3, with more in Q4. North American Q3 industry volume: tractors over 140 HP -5%, under 140 HP -12%, combines -13%. It also called the 2027 outlook 'uncertain'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for DE.
evidence.why_not_priced: It came after Deere last spoke. Previews do not cite it. The FY27 consensus of +29% already assumes a recovery, so it supports the street rather than beats it.
evidence.independence: The AEM October data (https://www.rfdtv.com/four-wheel-drive-tractor-sales-rise-despite-broader-equipment-weakness) point the same way for large tractors.
evidence.link: CNH is Deere's closest same-product competitor in North American large ag (tractors over 140 HP, combines). It sells into the same dealer channel and growers. CNH ag sales were $2.9bn in the quarter.

evidence.text: AGCO (Q3, 2026-10-29) cut its industry outlooks for Western Europe, Latin America and North America. Its CEO called it the weakest global industry demand in more than a decade. Net sales were -8.6%, but North America was +35% in constant currency.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for DE.
evidence.why_not_priced: AGCO's cut is public. Deere's own FY26 regional guides (US/Canada large ag and South America -15 to -20%, Europe flat) are already below. The relevance is FY27 Europe and South America, where Deere has not spoken.
evidence.independence: Abimaq Brazil data (finding 10) agree on South America. The AGCO 8-K is at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000075/a2026earningsreleaseq3.htm.
evidence.link: AGCO is a direct competitor in tractors and combines (Fendt, Massey Ferguson) in Europe, South America and North America. Its 2026 sales are about $9-10bn, against Deere's PPA and SAT exposure to the same regions.

evidence.text: AEM US data for October 2026 (Deere's fiscal Q4): 4WD tractors +7.7% y/y (337 against 313) and 100+ HP 2WD +3.2%, against YTD 4WD -19% and total tractors -11.6%. Combines -9.6% (YTD -9.1%). Large tractors turned positive in the last month of the quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is an industry unit proxy, widely available to ag analysts and not company-level. It is small, at 337 units.
evidence.independence: Proxy. CNH's Q3 over-140 HP figure (-5%, a smaller decline than under 140 HP) is consistent.

evidence.text: Sandhills (September 2026): used tractor (100+ HP) inventory -14.82% y/y, down for 16 consecutive months, with auction values +4.8% y/y. Used combine inventory -9.51% with auction values +2.74% y/y, but combine values are trending down month to month.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deere's CEO cited 'improved used inventories' as a bottoming signal on 2026-08-20, and the stock rose 6.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a proxy and public, consistent with management's August message. It supports a recovery guide rather than surprising.
evidence.independence: OptionBeast (2026-11-21, https://wp.optionbeast.com/2026/11/21/deere-reports-tuesday-the-fy2027-guide-is-what-counts/) says North American high-horsepower tractor and combine inventory is more than 50% below the mid-2024 peak. evidence.text: Brazilian ag machinery industry revenue (Abimaq) was -15.7% y/y in September 2026 and -21.6% YTD through September. Abimaq expects about -20% for 2026, citing high rates and deferred investment. That is weak carry-over into Deere's FY27 South America.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured.

evidence.independence: CNH's Q3 reports South America tractors -22% and combines -19%.

evidence.text: Caterpillar's Q3 2026 (2026-10-29): sales +17%, Construction Industries profit +33% ($1.83bn), and 'strong order rates and a record backlog'. Construction demand supports Deere's C&F, which is guided +20% in FY26 and running at a 12.1% margin.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 C&F +18% and +84% operating profit was the headline of the +6.9% August reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is widely known. CAT itself fell about 9.5% on its print, so construction strength is not a free pass.
evidence.independence: CNH's construction outlook was raised to +8-10% and North American construction demand is +10%. Deere raised construction production rates per Manufacturing Dive (2026-11-02).
evidence.link: Same end market and products (earthmoving and construction equipment, North American dealers). Deere C&F is about 30% of equipment operations sales (Q3: $3.62bn of $11.0bn).

evidence.text: Expectations have reset in price. The stock fell from $673.54 to $609.25 (-9.5%) between about 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-20 and sits about $617 into the print (5-day -5.0%), 13% below its September all-time high. evidence.why_not_priced: This runs against the options market (skew +14.5, downside paid). The case for it: the skew prices a guide below $23.40, and the buy-side has had a week and a public Bernstein note to move there. evidence.text: HPE's FY27 guide moderates Cloud & AI margin to about 14% from 15.2%. HPE closed +17.4% on Nov 23, then fell 6.7% after hours and about 16% on Nov 24 despite beating and raising revenue. That is a live analog for a Dell beat-and-raise being sold on the margin outlook.

evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced already: Dell fell about 10% on Nov 24 alongside HPE. What is not priced is whether Dell repeats the step-down. If the market were sure Dell would guide margins down like HPE, the skew would be steeper than +3.56 and the straddle would carry a larger downside premium.
evidence.independence: TrendForce's Q4 2026 DRAM contract outlook (separate source) points the same way on cost. Morgan Stanley's memory-cost downgrade is a 2025 story and is excluded.
evidence.link: Same products, same fiscal quarter, same memory suppliers; Dell guides Q4 (Nov-Jan) and HPE guided Q1 (Nov-Jan), the same calendar months.

evidence.text: TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices +10-15% q/q in 4Q26 and server DIMM contract prices +10%+ q/q, and its Oct 30 update says server DRAM prices kept climbing in October. evidence.why_not_priced: Industry series, public for weeks. Its transmission into Dell's Q4 margin guide depends on Dell's pass-through, which only the call reveals. If it were fully priced, HPE's similar commentary would not have taken that stock down 16%.

evidence.text: The Q4 2026 guide, GOTU's first statement on that period, is more likely than not to land at or above the street's implied Q4. next_guide.company_current_guide: None for FY27. The 2026-09-21 8-K withholds FY27 guidance and assumes calendar-2027 industry PC units fall roughly mid-single digits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000047217/000114036126037170/ef20082499_form8k.htm). On the Q3 call: input costs rise in FY27 at a slower rate, and the PS margin goes back to its long-term range as quickly as possible.
next_guide.basis: The first FY27 guide is likely to come in below the $3.15 street midpoint, for four reasons. FY26's $3.19-3.29 includes $0.19 of tariff refunds. Intel's 2027 unit view (-10%) is about twice HP's own assumption. TrendForce has PC DRAM still rising 13-18% in 4Q26, with Korean suppliers cutting PC DRAM output by more than 20% in 2027. And last year HP opened FY26 at $2.90-3.20, below the street. Against that: management says Q4 is the margin trough, and Lenovo held a 7.1% PC margin.

evidence.text: Intel (HP's main CPU supplier) said on 2026-10-29 that industry PC units fall about 12% in 2026 and about 10% in 2027. HP's own 8-K of 2026-09-21 assumed calendar-2027 units decline only 'roughly mid-single-digits'. Yet the street's FY27 EPS ($3.15) and revenue (+0.4%) have not moved in 30 or 60 days, so HP's first FY27 guide is built on a unit outlook about twice as bad as HP last said.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: When HP issued its first FY26 guide (2025-11-25, $2.90-3.20 against a higher street), the stock fell 1.4% (baseline). The 2026-09-21 8-K with the mid-single-digit unit assumption cost -2% intraday (https://finviz.com/news/393837/hp-shares-fall-2-as-company-anticipates-pc-market-contraction-in-2027).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock has partly priced it: -9.5% on 2026-10-30 and -17% over six sessions. The sell-side has not: FY27 EPS sits at $3.15, the same as 30 and 60 days ago. If estimates had absorbed Intel's view, the FY27 average would have fallen and revenue would show a decline, not +0.4%. The open question is whether HP's guide resets the estimates.
evidence.independence: HP's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000047217/000114036126037170/ef20082499_form8k.htm) gives the mid-single-digit comparison. The Intel drop and its spillover to HP and Dell are reported independently (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/hpq/news/why-up-down/why-hp-hpq-shares-are-sliding-today). Shares its guide target with the FY27 guide-arithmetic finding below, but rests on a different fact.
evidence.link: Intel supplies the x86 CPUs in most HP PCs; Intel's client unit view is a read on the same end market and on OEM order books, including HP's.

evidence.text: FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $3.19-3.29 includes $0.19 of tariff refunds ($0.08 in Q4), which leaves an underlying base of about $3.00-3.10. The street's FY27 $3.15 therefore assumes underlying EPS growth in a year when Intel sees units -10%, management expects input costs to keep rising, and PS margins start below their 5-7% range. Last year HP opened FY26 at $2.90-3.20, below the street.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-guide prints: 2025-11-25 -1.4% close to close, despite an 'up 12% over the following week' path (https://www.aol.com/articles/hp-inc-earnings-preview-wall-183506855.html). 2025-02-27 -6.82% and 2025-05-28 -8.27%, both guide-led cuts (baseline).

If the market expected the refunds to roll off into a lower FY27, the estimate would have drifted down after the 8-K and after Intel. The put skew suggests the options market expects something like this, so the size is held down. FY27 consensus has only one source, so the size is capped.
evidence.independence: The refund amounts come from the FQ3 press release (https://finviz.com/news/385926/hp-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results). The FY27 street figure comes from Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HPQ/analysis). Shares the transcript with the Q4 trough claims.

evidence.text: IDC (2026-10-08) has HP calendar-Q3 PC units at 10.3M, -30.9% y/y, with share down from 19.1% to 16.5%, against an industry -20.1%; Gartner also has HP at -30.9%. HP's Q4 guide (Aug-Oct) assumed industry units down 'high-teens' and revenue up y/y. The street's FQ4 revenue of $15.3-15.47B (+4.5-5.7%) needs PS revenue of about +8% on units of about -28%, which means PS ASP up about 50% against about 40% in FQ3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: HP has beaten revenue every quarter of FY26 (FQ3 PS revenue $11.8B against about $10.5B consensus), and the stock still fell on those prints (baseline -1.88% and -2.92%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's FQ4 revenue average has not fallen: $15.30B on Yahoo, $15.47B on EW. If the -31% unit figure had been carried into models, the FQ4 average would sit near or below the year-ago $14.64B. IDC blames earlier pull-ins, so the sell-in drop may overstate HP's own fiscal-quarter sell-in. That is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Gartner's 2026-10-12 release also has HP at -30.9% (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps; fetch 403, snippet only). Lenovo's revenue print (finding below) points the other way, which is why this proxy is sized below it.

evidence.text: Lenovo, the #1 PC vendor, reported on 2026-11-19 for July-September, after HP last spoke. IDG revenue was +15% y/y to $17.4B with operating margin 7.1%, described as 'well maintained', while its units fell 22.6% in IDC's data. Price is offsetting units and PC margins are holding at the market leader.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: HP's PS revenue beat by about 12% in FQ3, the margin came in at 4.6% (below range, as guided), and the stock fell 2.9%. Good PS revenue alone has not lifted it.
evidence.why_not_priced: HPQ's 5-day change is -0.44%, so Lenovo's release did not move it; the stock still sits near its post-Intel low. If the market had read Lenovo as clearing HP's revenue and margin risk, HPQ would have recovered part of the Intel gap. Lenovo's IDG includes phones, which dilutes the read.
evidence.independence: Unit figure from IDC (https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26). The margin figure is from the 36Kr analysis via search (https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4076212792711041).
evidence.link: Same product and channel: Lenovo (23.8% unit share) and HP (16.5%) are #1 and #2 in IDC's 3Q26 table, and Lenovo's fiscal Q2 overlaps two of HP's three FQ4 months. HP's FQ4 PS is about 75% of revenue.

evidence.text: TrendForce (2026-11-11) sees PC DRAM contract prices +13-18% q/q in 4Q26, down from +18-23% in 3Q26. That supports HP's claim that Q4 is the margin trough. But costs are still rising, OEM and North American channel finished-goods inventory is building, OEMs are cutting 4Q26-1Q27 SSD and DRAM procurement, and Korean suppliers plan to cut PC DRAM output by more than 20% in 2027. Net: a constrained FY27 cost line and a weak FQ1 sell-in.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Memory-cost commentary drove the -2.92% (FQ3) and -1.88% (FQ2) reactions to EPS beats (https://invezz.com/news/2026/08/27/hp-stock-slides-5-as-memory-costs-pressure-pc-margins/).

evidence.independence: The deceleration matches HP's own 'slower rate' language in the Q3 transcript. The inventory build matches IDC's 'channels worried about too much inventory' (https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26).
evidence.link: Memory and storage are about 35% of HP's PC bill of materials (HP CFO, reported https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/hp-says-memory-costs-doubled-to-35-percent-of-pc-build-materials-in-one-quarter); TrendForce tracks the contract prices HP pays.

evidence.text: Q3 gross margin is set up to step up from Q2's 11.0%. At the Q2 call the CFO said margins would expand further in H2 on higher-priced Livis variants, refreshed BEVs and the i9. evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus still carries a RMB942m loss, which implies a margin well below DB's 16.7%. If the market had priced DB's view, the loss consensus would have narrowed toward RMB300m and the stock would not have fallen 15% since Nov 11. The margin bar is single-sourced, so this is capped small.
evidence.independence: CFO H2 margin-expansion comment: https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/26/li-auto-earnings-q2-2026/ (a different document from DB's note). The Earnings Whispers preview names memory, battery and PCB cost inflation as the offset.

evidence.text: On 2026-11-12 Nanox signed a Yorkville Standby Equity Purchase Agreement: up to $10.0M primary at 97% of the lowest daily VWAP over a three-day pricing period (registering ~31.4M advance shares at $0.318, ~40% of the 78.75M outstanding) plus a $40M resale SEPA and 1.22M commitment shares; the first 725,600 shares were sold to Yorkville on 2026-11-18 at $0.3132 for $227k, with shares outstanding at 80.39M. Asked what the money buys: survival under a going-concern flag, not a ramp (Q3 revenue flat q/q at $4.3-4.4M, no change in ARC deployments), so it signs negative, and the pricing formula rewards Yorkville for selling into any print-day rally.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The SEPA 6-K day (2026-11-12) the stock fell -12.64% (sealed baseline history) and it is -28.75% over the five sessions since the first advance; the August $8M registered direct at $1.00 preceded the slide from ~$1 to $0.40 by mid-October.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 5-day -29% is consistent with Yorkville distribution. What is not priced is the print-day mechanic: any rally on the call gives Yorkville a fresh, higher VWAP to sell advances into, so upside is capped while the first-day reaction is open; if this were fully priced, the stock would have stabilised after the first tranche rather than sliding a further ~30% to $0.205.
evidence.independence: 424B5 supplement no. 1 dated 2026-11-23 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1795251/000121390026122954/ea0313197-424b5_nanox.htm) confirms the first tranche and the 80,388,806 share count; Yorkville 13G 2026-11-13. Same issuer documents, different filings.

evidence.text: The adjourned special general meeting is at 07:00 ET on 2026-11-25, 90 minutes before the call, and votes on a reverse split framework of 1-for-20 to 1-for-50 and on raising authorized share capital by 200M to 350M shares ([sizing note removed]; the 8.33% holder Moshe Moalem has contractually agreed to vote for both, so passage is likely and the result reaches the market inside the window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reverse split or authorization vote at this company found; the meeting was originally set for 2026-11-18 and postponed a week, during which the stock fell from ~$0.31 to ~$0.21.
evidence.why_not_priced: The vote is public, so the direction is largely priced; what is not is the confirmation of headroom: with 80M shares out and 150M authorized today, approval more than doubles what can be issued to Yorkville and others, which a $0.21 stock with a 1:20-1:50 split pending usually trades down on. If fully priced, there would be no further drift after the 18 Nov postponement, and there has been.
evidence.independence: Revised proxy card (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795251/000121390026118528/ea031149901ex99-2.htm) and the original 2026-10-28 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795251/000121390026113380/ea030999302ex99-1.htm); one filing set.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue will print at the pre-released ~$4.3-4.4M (teleradiology ~$3.1M flat, imaging systems/OEM ~$0.3M, AI/software ~$1.0M mostly Health IT consolidation) against a stale street consensus of ~$5.44-5.5M, so headline services will show a ~20% revenue miss on a number the company already disclosed.

evidence.why_not_priced: The number itself is priced (pre-released five weeks ago); the only unpriced part is the mechanical 'misses by $1M' headline from estimate services that never revised, which can hit a thin, retail-held tape at 07:00 ET.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers 2026-11-18 states the same guide-vs-consensus gap (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NNOX/23257); Benzinga consensus $5.5M (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/NNOX/earnings-forecasts).

evidence.text: Into the print the stock is -28.75% over 5 sessions and -36.07% over 20 to a 52-week low of $0.205, a ~$16.8M market cap against ~$26.0M of cash and deposits at 30 Sep (before an estimated ~$11-14M of Q4 burn), so the market already discounts heavy dilution and a near-zero equity; the bar to rise is low on any burn or funding news.

evidence.why_not_priced: It is the price; the finding is that the drawdown is explained by Yorkville supply rather than by an unpriced deterioration, which leaves room for a relief move if the call quantifies burn cuts. Shrunk because the explanation for the drawdown (financing supply) persists through the window.
evidence.independence: Sealed baseline tape (run_up_5d -28.75, run_up_20d -36.07, pct_from_52w_low 0.0); cash from the 2026-10-16 pre-release (https://finviz.com/news/403663/nanox-provides-business-update-and-furnishes-certain-preliminary-unaudited-financial-data-for-third-quarter-ended-september-30-2026).

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The plan's announcement was followed by +59.8% on 2026-11-10 on 108x normal volume, fully reversed after the SEPA; restructuring payments are flagged to raise near-term cash outflows.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline target is public and its spike was given back, so what remains unpriced is the quantification (a dollar burn figure or a signed divestiture). If the market believed in a smaller burn, the stock would not trade at ~0.65x September cash.

next_guide.basis: Nine-month volume is 44,790 (+0.6%). Meeting a 2-5% full-year guide needs about 16,500-18,300 cars in Q4 against 15,608 in Q4 2025 and 14,371 in Q3 2026. Ex-US Q3 fell 8%, US new-car sales end with MY2026 inventory, and the Polestar 4 SUV only starts deliveries in Q4. A cut, or a guide at the bottom of the range, is the likelier outcome.

evidence.text: Arithmetic on the company's own numbers makes a second 2026 volume guide cut likely. The guide is 'low to mid single digit' growth on 60,119 cars in 2025, which needs about 61,300-63,100 cars. Nine months delivered 44,790, so Q4 would need 16,500-18,300, which is +6% to +17% on Q4 2025's 15,608. Q3 was 14,371 with ex-US down 8% (12,211), and the US contributed about 2,160 cars in Q3 from a channel that ends with MY2026 inventory.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guide cut (2026-09-03, volume from low double digits to low-to-mid single digits) moved the stock -27.5% on the day.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -88% from its high and a Sell consensus exists. But the FY revenue consensus of $3.18B still implies H2 revenue 34% above H1 on flat volume, so the street's numbers have not absorbed a second cut. If they had, the FY consensus would sit near $2.7-2.8B.
evidence.independence: Guide and 2025 base from https://electrive.com/2026/09/04/polestar-lowers-forecasts-amid-weak-half-year-figures and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260109689366/en/Polestar-reports-record-retail-sales-in-2025 . The CEO said Europe was 'somewhat flat' this year (https://eletric-vehicles.com/geely/polestar/polestar-has-built-first-5000-polestar-4-suvs-in-south-korea-ceo-says/). Shares the volume-release document with the reported-quarter finding.

evidence.text: The Q3 release must disclose the covenant and funding position, and the amended 2026 covenants look out of reach. The club loan carries a minimum quarterly cash of EUR400m, a debt-to-asset ratio (Q2 actual 1.47:1 against an amended cap of 1.50:1), and a reported 2026 minimum revenue of $3.30B. H1 revenue was $1.36B and even the street's FY figure is $3.18B. Cash was $888M at June 30 after H1 operating cash outflow of $850M, and only $100M of the 3 Sep $400M Geely loan is committed. A waiver or amendment, new support, or a breach has to be addressed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Going-concern language first appeared with H1 (2026-09-03, -27.5%, mixed with the guide cut). No clean reaction to a funding-only item.
evidence.why_not_priced: The going-concern risk is broadly known, but the market cannot see whether the Q2-Q3 test passed or whether lenders waived it. An unresolved binary would trade like this one, with an indefinite delay and a 43% slide, and it resolves on this print. Sign: a waiver plus a committed Geely facility is a relief; a breach or a new dilutive equity raise at ~$2.8 is a further leg down. The money buys runway, not a demand ramp (Q3 volume +1%), so the lean stays negative.
evidence.independence: The $3.30B revenue floor and the Chinese-loan 30,000-car H1 test, cleared by 423 cars, are from https://eletric-vehicles.com/geely/polestar/polestar-cleared-a-loan-covenant-by-423-cars-sec-filing-shows/ (snippet only; 403 on fetch). The Geely term loan with only Term A committed is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1884082/000110465926105064/tm2624554d1_6k.htm . Covenant arithmetic is inference from documents.

evidence.text: Polestar postponed the Q3 release two days before the 5 Nov date 'to allow more time to conclude its quarter-end closing process' and gave no date until 23 Nov. That points to judgemental items in the close, such as impairments, inventory NRV, US exit provisions or the going-concern assessment. H1 already said 'additional costs and charges may arise' on the US exit, which cost about $211M in H1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The postponement day (2026-11-05, the original print date) closed -13.6% after a +7.5% day; Polestar's 2024 delays ended in a restatement of 2021-2022 accounts.
evidence.why_not_priced: The delay is priced as uncertainty, but the size of any charge is not known. An unquantified reported-quarter impairment is the kind of item that has paid before. If it were known, the release-day move would be set by the guide alone.
evidence.independence: The US-exit charge and 'may arise' wording are in https://www.webull.com/news/15514532644512768 (H1 call transcript). Hurbra (https://hurbra.se/?p=50868, 2026-11-16) notes the company cited no accounting or audit problem. Related to the covenant finding, because the going-concern assessment sits in the same close.

evidence.why_not_priced: The street sits at the guide midpoint and the preview frames the risk as a miss. A market pricing the guide record would show a consensus above RMB450m, or a whisper above $0.46. Neither exists. The size is small because the result lands inside what the company already guided.

evidence.text: CEO Haisheng Wu stepped down on 2026-09-20. Chief Risk Officer Yan Zheng (CRO since 2020, 18 years in consumer-finance risk) became CEO effective 2026-09-21, so this is the first print and the first guide under a risk-officer CEO. That raises the chance of heavier Q3 provisioning or a conservative Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-21 6-K session in the baseline moved -1.98%, a small reaction to the announcement itself. No prior print under this CEO.
evidence.why_not_priced: The announcement was priced as a personnel event (-2%). How a new CEO sets his first guide is only visible tonight. If it were priced, the street would show a Q4 number below the Q3 range, and no Q4 street figure was found. This is an inference about behaviour, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Chinese coverage confirms Wu moves to the international business and Zheng, a risk specialist, takes over: https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260925/c680282628.shtml and https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3782228. Same event, different reporters.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call management said: August FPD3/FPD7 up about 20% MoM; August C-M2 guided up about 25% sequentially, with C-M2 up noticeably in Q3; normalisation 'will probably still take at least two to three quarters'; external funding cost up about 25bp in July-August and expected to trend up in H2; volume will not return to Q2 levels soon. That points to a Q4 guide held around the depressed Q3 level, not a recovery.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line decides this stock: the Q2 2026 guide cut gave -18.91% and the Q1 2026 guide gave +25.02%.
evidence.why_not_priced: These statements are public and partly priced, since the stock is down 52% since.
